title: Customer privacy service intake matrix and response runway
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide variety of non-bug data governance requests (log redaction, retention changes, PII removal, audit export formats). We lack a concise operator-friendly intake matrix that (1) scores requests by technical effort and compliance risk, (2) surfaces required approvals and SLAs, and (3) maps to an actionable response runway for PM/Eng/Security/GTM.

Goal: Deliver a pragmatic intake matrix + response runway and an operator runbook that lets SRE/Support/CS triage and respond to enterprise data-control requests consistently within defined SLOs. The artifact should reduce decision latency, clarify approval gates, and produce clear next actions (work request, policy change, or customer config).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A one-page intake matrix that scores requests along axes: business sensitivity, PII exposure, systems touched (runtime/logging/audit), engineering effort estimate band, and recommended SLA tier.

A2: Response runway with three canonical paths: Configable customer-side change (no engineering), Short-scope eng task (<=2w), Project-level change (requires cross-functional project plan). Each path includes approvers, expected timeline, and rollback criteria.
A3: Operator runbook with triage checklist, sample email/Slack responses, escalation contact list, and mapping to existing change request forms (Confluence + GH templates).
A4: Integration notes for Support UI flags (ticket tags) and a simple webhook spec for forwarding high-risk requests to Security/Legal.
A5: Stakeholder review completed (Security, Legal, SRE, Support, Solutions) and sign-off recorded in the Confluence doc.
A6: Three pilot tickets processed using the new matrix and runbook with retrospective notes captured and two improvements planned for iteration.
A7: Metrics defined to surface in Console: median time-to-first-response, percent of requests auto-routable to non-eng path, and number of policy-change requests queued.
A8: No open security review blockers flagged by SEC team before soft rollout.
runbook_steps: Step 0: Intake — Support tags incoming ticket with label 'enterprise-data-control' and fills minimal intake form (customer, request type, urgency, example logs).
Step 1: Automatic scoring — Use rule-based scorer to assign sensitivity/effort band. If sensitivity == high OR PII present -> auto-notify Security + Legal.
Step 2: Decision gate — Apply matrix: route to 'config' path if effort_band == 0 and no policy change needed; otherwise assign to 'short-scope eng' or 'project'.
Step 3: Approvals — Short-scope requires PM + SRE approval; Project requires PM + Security + Legal + Engineering manager OK. Record approval in Confluence checklist template.
Step 4: Execution — Create GH epic/issue per path and tag with release and customer-impact metadata. For redaction/retention changes, attach data retention compliance checklist.
Step 5: Verification & Communication — Once change deploys, verify with sample logs/exports and notify customer using templated language. Update ticket and metrics dashboard.
Step 6: Postmortem — For any request that escalates to project, run a 1-week retro capturing root cause and opportunity to reduce operator time.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: we prefer a deterministic rule-based intake scorer for now vs. ML due to explainability and auditability. If we later need ML, it will be a separate initiative.
Edge cases: multi-tenant redaction where redaction rules may conflict with per-customer settings — flagged as a Project-level task requiring Dedicated/Private deployment considerations.
Conservative SLA bands recommended: 48 hours first response for high-sensitivity requests, 10 business days for short-scope eng tasks, and project timelines negotiated per contract.
Decision: Do not expose automated redaction tooling to customer-facing UI until Security signs off on test harness and verification steps.
